These burners are great for replacing the new yet crappy elements all new stoves are equipped with which do not work (thanks UL for your gross stupidity). My only complaint with these eyes is the fact that the coils are not flat which means you may have hot and cold spots on your light weight cookware. Heavy pots and pans will press the coils flat for even cooking but small and light weight pots and pans may tend to float over uneven coils. If not for this issue, I would have given them 5 stars. All in all, they are still well worth the money to fix the problem introduced by UL's unenforceable mandate.

One of the first thing I noticed with these elements that I hardly noticed with the factory elements is that after a few seconds of turning on the burner I could actually feel the heat coming off of them. I hardly ever noticed the heat with the original elements.

I will add that if you have been using the defunct elements for a long time, you may also need to replace the switches (especially f you have a GE stove), as the original (so called) safety elements, may have also damaged the thermal circuit in the switches as well. So if you still have problems controlling the temperature after replacing the elements, you may need switches as well.

The speed is about 2 cups per hour,  or about 2-3 hours to fill the basket.  Overall the fan is a bit noisy,  so you might want to place it in out of the way,  or on the back porch,  but you will need to be refilling it constantly if you hope to yield 33 lbs per day.  The black rubber feet leave marks on a white countertop,  so you may want to place a placemat or something under the feet.  They are black rubber and will mark your countertop, which can be scrubbed off,  but it's just something to note.  Try to use filtered water,  i noticed the reservoir and inside smelled like chlorine,  so that's probably because I used tap water,  so for best results filter your water.  The reason we bought this was mainly for camping,  I plan to run this off an inverter (which could kill a car battery FYI)  or small 1000W genset to provide us ice for our drinks and coolers,  so your power source needs to be constant - it's not practical to run your car for hours just to make ice.  When we go to our local music festival in the Summer (Merritt) they charge $8/bag for ice which is outrageous,  and we expect this unit will pay for itself after just 2 x 3-day camping trips, at least we have some options now.  Despite finding a power source and the effort filling with water over and over,  and emptying the ice into bags for cooling food,  it will be handy at our parties too,  and reduces people messing around in the fridge.
